decisions.reason: Because it moved from a mere mention in 2023 to its own page in 2024 and fits the firm's core geospatial integration offer, management would likely judge it as at least near aspiration and keep it while exploiting complementarities with existing projects.

Although its visibility did not deepen beyond a website mention, the framework is close to the firm's strategic core of open, extensible geospatial solutions, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it for now given its platform value and the firm's R&D capability, but with clear caution because market feedback appears weaker than for peers in the portfolio.

Its stronger 2024 presentation and clear positioning for integrating GeoIT into existing user-management systems suggest performance at or above aspiration, so management would keep it as a promising extension of the established business.

As a newly launched workshop closely tied to the firm's consulting and training strengths, it likely requires limited slack to maintain and would be kept while management waits for more demand evidence rather than dropping it prematurely.
